date_note: Cyber Kendra's page is dated Nov 20 but states the situation as of Nov 19; published date taken as Nov 19.
title: FastUnlock: unpatched Windows 11 Narrator flaw lets an attacker with physical access bypass the lock screen and BitLocker, researcher claims
summary: A researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse or Nightmare-Eclipse posted "FastUnlock" on GitHub "without prior coordination", Cyber Kendra says, claiming a Narrator lock-screen flaw lets someone with physical access get past BitLocker on Windows 11 26H2. ThreatLocker's proof of concept ran code without signing in, as a non-administrator account; The Hacker News says it does not break the encryption. As of November 19 there was no CVE or Microsoft fix, per Cyber Kendra.
plain: A researcher says a lost or stolen Windows 11 laptop could be unlocked using the screen reader feature. Microsoft has published no fix or advisory yet.
exec: Matters for lost or stolen laptops that rely on BitLocker; physical access is required and no attacks in the wild are reported.
action: Until Microsoft responds: ThreatLocker says a BitLocker preboot PIN helps on a device that was just turned on; the researcher suggests blocking Narrator on the lock screen with AppLocker or a restrictive DACL (test first). Keep devices physically secured.

sources.name: ThreatLocker: Proof of concept for FastUnlock Windows lock screen bypass from Nightmare Eclipse
ThaiCERT: alert on the FastUnlock zero-day in Windows (Thai)

key_findings: No CVE as of Nov 19; no Microsoft advisory, fix or workaround listed.
Needs physical access and at least one account on the PC linked to an online Microsoft account, per Cyber Kendra.
Researcher suggests blocking Narrator via AppLocker or a custom DACL as a possible fix.
recommendations: Secure devices physically; consider blocking Narrator until a patch ships.

validation.note: Cyber Kendra and Security Affairs report the researcher's release and claims. ThreatLocker's own post (Nov 19) reproduces it: code runs from the lock screen as the non-administrator WSIAccount user with physical access; it names a BitLocker preboot PIN as mitigation. The Hacker News says encryption is not broken. No Microsoft confirmation, CVE or fix on the pages read; no in-the-wild use reported. Still a claim. Update 2026-11-23: ThaiCERT's alert (23 Nov, read) says Microsoft has no patch yet and no evidence of real-world attacks has been found; it advises a BitLocker Startup PIN, shutting down or hibernating unattended devices (a lock screen alone is not enough) and physical security. It does not say Microsoft confirmed the flaw and gives no CVE. Still a claim.

review.note: stronger than source: 'without coordinating with Microsoft' -> 'without prior coordination' (Cyber Kendra); encryption/sign-in statements attributed; added published days
